scope: One disposable Lighting slice, one CLI-created mood, one CLI Q2 edit, native Save As to a new path and a fresh-process reopen. Not a generic executor completion or whole-family qualification.

provenance.raw_evidence: Private case retains CLI outputs, project snapshots, selected raw transport replies, reopened-editor capture, SSH restart/final-state receipts and exact comparisons. Direct SDK operation acknowledgements remain in the originating session transcript. No vendor project, screenshot, endpoint or credential is published.

workflow: Reuse a pinned disposable Lighting slice with four direct moods and collection Num=4, Outputs=18.
Run config add-mood with neither identity override, name Workflow 20261111 lox-ue95 and color hsv(300,100,30), saving to a new file.
Run config set-mood-color on that new mood with output-index 2 and hsv(120,100,10), saving to another new file.
Transfer exact CLI-saved bytes and open the owned file in the pinned native application.
After an explicitly requested MCP restart, reconcile the unchanged original Config process and file. Stop on USER_CONTROL, obtain explicit user handoff and resume under normal control gates.
Ctrl+S leaves original bytes identical. Use the normal Save As dialog, verify the new absolute filename and absent destination, then save to that new path.
Capture native-produced bytes, exit normally, verify Config count zero and reopen the exact new output in a fresh process.
Open the controller editor and select the new mood for observation only. Cancel, exit normally and verify all saved bytes unchanged and Config count zero.

checks.CLI_creation: All baseline bytes are restored exactly by removing only the one new scene line, restoring collection Num=4 from 5 and reverting the two individually recorded Document Date/DateS attributes. No sorting, metadata-ignore list, XML sanitization or reference normalization.
checks.CLI_edit: Only the new mood Q2 changes from 1610612736 to 1610622736, plus individually recorded Document Date/DateS spellings. All other raw bytes are exact.
checks.native_output: The actual newly created Save As output equals the complete CLI-edited file byte-for-byte; the structured CLI Lighting inspections also agree exactly.

outputs.high_type_nibbles: 0x60000000 for Q1/Q2/Q10; zero for other new outputs. Preserved exactly, without interpreting a nibble as a physical channel role.

checks.reopened_editor: The new mood name is visible and selectable with displayed ID 1 and input T5/1. This is native model recognition, not just unchanged bytes after launch.
checks.unrelated_data: All existing moods, controller attributes, channels, IDs, references, nested/sequence data, unknown attributes, ordering, BOM, line endings and remaining file bytes equal the CLI-saved input.
checks.cleanup: Both Config instances exited normally; final Config count zero. Existing offline firewall fence remained enabled. The requested restarted manual MCP task remains running.

limits: The fixture's numeric dimmer controls display 100 for both RGB-packed Q1 and Q2 values. This observation does not validate color rendering or interpret arbitrary packed color values as dimmer brightness.
Ctrl+S and the new Save As output were byte-identical to input. No claim that every serializer branch ran, a dirty native model was serialized, or accepted native edits preserve these values.
Editor inspection was cancelled after the save/reopen comparison. Opening it is not assumed pure; no save followed, and unchanged disk bytes do not prove whole-model cancellation rollback.

One nonempty, 18-output fixture and one automatic identity allocation do not establish gap/exhaustion/collision, sparse-output, import-reconciliation, CID-edit, sequence-edit, runtime, hardware or full-family parity.
MCP restart, management and SDK readiness are not platform qualification. No VM admission, new extraction, infrastructure policy change or generic automation rewrite.
Times are retained per source; no shared-clock or elapsed-time inference.
